questions.question: To prevent a rollover, cargo should be:

options.text: Loaded with most weight on the driver's side of the trailer.
Placed near the rear of the trailer.
Spread out evenly in the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spread out evenly in the trailer.
questions.explanation: Cargo weight must be spread evenly throughout the trailer. Do not put too much weight on one side.

questions.question: A trailer that is too high:
questions.explanation: The trailer must be at the right height before coupling. If it is too high, it may not couple correctly. If it is too low, the trailer nose may be damaged.

questions.question: Trailers made after ____ must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).
questions.explanation: Trailers and converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS).

questions.question: Which vehicle type is most likely to experience the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: Double and triple combinations are most likely to roll over from the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: If you are unsure if a trailer has ABS, you can:

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors connected to the back of the brakes.
Drive on a slippery surface and see if ABS activates.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors connected to the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers made on or after March 1, 1998 must have ABS. A yellow warning light indicates ABS. For older trailers, check underneath for wires and sensors connected to the brakes to see if ABS is present.

questions.question: A lightly-loaded vehicle stops more slowly than a fully-loaded vehicle because:

options.text: The stiff suspension and strong brakes will have good traction.
The stiff suspension and strong brakes will have poor traction.
The brakes only work when a trailer reaches a minimum weight.
The suspension only works when a trailer reaches a minimum weight.

questions.correctAnswerText: The stiff suspension and strong brakes will have poor traction.
questions.explanation: An empty vehicle stops more slowly than a loaded one. With less weight, the suspension and brakes have less traction on the road.

questions.question: To reduce the risk of a rollover, you should:

options.text: Load cargo as far forward as possible.
Load cargo as far back as possible.
Load cargo as low as possible.
Stack cargo as high as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Load cargo as low as possible.
questions.explanation: Keep cargo as close to the ground as possible. Also take curves and corners slowly to reduce rollover risk.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: It allows wheels to lock up.
It prevents wheels from locking up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It prevents wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: ABS helps prevent wheel lockup during hard braking. If ABS detects wheels are about to lock, it reduces braking pressure to a safe level.

questions.question: If color-coded, what color identifies service lines?
questions.explanation: Air lines are sometimes color-coded. Blue is used for service lines and red is used for emergency lines.

questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.explanation: The service line is also called the control line or signal line.

questions.question: What happens when you push in the trailer air supply control?

options.text: It turns off the air brakes.
It supplies air to the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It supplies air to the trailer.
questions.explanation: Pushing in the trailer air supply control sends air to the trailer. Pulling it out stops the air supply and activates the emergency brakes.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?
questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when you turn too fast. To avoid them, drive slowly on ramps and around corners. Avoid quick lane changes when pulling a trailer.

questions.question: What is true about combination vehicles?

options.text: They often have taller trailers than single trucks.
They are usually lighter than single trucks.
They require more skill to drive than single trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: They require more skill to drive than single trucks.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more skill to drive than single trucks. They are longer, heavier, and more likely to roll over.

questions.question: What does a tractor protection valve do?

options.text: It keeps air in the brake system if there is a serious leak.
It stops the truck from being stolen.
It prevents the driver from driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: It keeps air in the brake system if there is a serious leak.
questions.explanation: A tractor protection valve keeps air in the brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a serious leak. It closes automatically when pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: When driving a combination vehicle, what is best?
questions.explanation: Brake early and look far ahead to avoid sudden stops. This helps prevent your trailer from jackknifing.

questions.question: If you must back a trailer on a curve, which direction should you back?

options.text: Swerve back and forth while backing.

questions.explanation: Back toward the driver's side so you can see better. This gives you the best view while backing.

questions.question: What is the trailer hand valve used for?

options.text: To check the connection between trailer and tractor.

questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes.

questions.question: What happens if a trailer is too high when coupling?

options.text: It will not make a difference.
The coupling will be more secure.

questions.explanation: The trailer must be at the right height to couple properly. If it is too low, the trailer nose can be damaged. If it is too high, it may not couple correctly.

questions.question: What happens if you lose air pressure in the emergency line?
questions.explanation: When air pressure in the emergency line drops, the tractor protection valve closes and the emergency trailer brakes activate. This protects the air system if the trailer breaks away or leaks.

questions.question: If the trailer spring brakes do not release when you push the tractor air supply control, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the engine off and on again.

questions.explanation: All equipment must work properly before you drive. If the trailer spring brakes do not release, make sure the air line connections are properly attached and sealed.
